evidenceAudit.scope: Head injury and traumatic brain injury in adults and children in India from prehospital care to discharge: Glasgow Coma Scale (GCS) grading, airway, breathing and circulation, computed tomography (CT) indications, admission and surgical criteria, raised intracranial pressure (ICP) treatment, seizure prophylaxis and discharge, built on the ICMR Neurosurgery STW for Head Injury (July 2024).
findings: GCS bands (13–15 mild, 9–12 moderate, 3–8 severe), CT indications, red flags, prehospital ABC and transfer, admission criteria, extradural haematoma above 30 cc and subdural haematoma above 10 mm with midline shift above 5 mm for surgery, PaCO2 30–35 mmHg, head-end elevation, mannitol 20% 200 mL (adults) only if systolic BP above 90 mmHg, mannitol 0.25–1 g/kg, 3% saline 3 mL/kg 8-hourly, phenytoin 20 mg/kg then 5 mg/kg/day, levetiracetam 500 mg twice daily for 1–3 months, steroids not useful, repeat CT at 24 hours checked against the ICMR Neurosurgery STW (July 2024).
unverifiedSections: The STW gives no SpO2 or blood-pressure target beyond systolic above 90 mmHg before mannitol.
Tranexamic acid and analgesic doses are not given in the STW and are not included.
Children's mannitol dose is described as weight-based without a number; the 0.25–1 g/kg range is used.
The STW gives two PaCO2 ranges (30–35 and 30–32 mmHg); 30–35 mmHg is shown.
Drug cautions, contraindications and renal or hepatic adjustment lines without a source tag are general pharmacology statements and need formulary confirmation.

pathophysiology.summary: Traumatic brain injury (TBI) is a leading cause of death and disability among young people in India, mostly from road traffic crashes and falls. The primary injury happens at impact; much of the harm that follows is secondary injury from hypoxia, hypotension, raised intracranial pressure and seizures, which good early care prevents. The ICMR workflow asks for ABC stabilisation in the golden hour, a search for other injuries, GCS grading, early non-contrast CT with cervical spine imaging, admission for those at risk, osmotherapy for clinical signs of raised ICP once systolic BP is above 90 mmHg, and urgent neurosurgical referral for operable haematomas.
keyMechanisms: Primary injury: contusion, diffuse axonal injury and haematomas at impact.
Secondary injury: hypoxia, hypotension, hypercarbia and seizures worsen brain damage.
Expanding haematoma or oedema raises ICP and reduces cerebral perfusion, leading to herniation.
Osmotic agents draw water out of the brain to lower ICP.

physicalSigns: Scalp wound, skull fracture, cerebrospinal fluid leak
redFlags: Unconscious; irregular respiration; asymmetric pupils (ICMR STW)
Falling GCS, new focal deficit (ICMR STW)
precipitants: Road traffic crashes, often without helmet

differentials.distinguishingFeatures: May coexist; never assume it explains low GCS.

diagnosticCriteria.threshold: GCS below 15, transient loss of consciousness, suspected skull fracture, post-traumatic seizure, focal deficit, persistent vomiting, amnesia.
Extradural haematoma above 30 cc; subdural haematoma above 10 mm thick with midline shift above 5 mm and deterioration.

ruleIn.expectedFinding: Fall in GCS; unequal or unreactive pupils

clinicalManagement.title: Prehospital and arrival
actions: ABC per trauma guidelines; control external bleeding; immobilise the cervical spine (ICMR STW).
Transfer once ABC stable to a centre with CT and a neurosurgeon (ICMR STW).

clinicalManagement.title: Assess and image
actions: GCS, pupils, focal signs; search for other injuries (ICMR STW).
Non-contrast CT head with cervical spine imaging (ICMR STW).

clinicalManagement.title: Raised ICP
actions: Elevate the head end; sedation and analgesia; PaCO2 30–35 mmHg if ventilated (ICMR STW).
Mannitol only if systolic BP above 90 mmHg and red flags; or 3% saline (ICMR STW).

clinicalManagement.title: Surgery
actions: Extradural above 30 cc or subdural above 10 mm with shift above 5 mm and deterioration: neurosurgery (ICMR STW).
Decompressive craniectomy by a neurosurgeon only (ICMR STW).

clinicalManagement.title: Admit or discharge
actions: Admit: amnesia, loss of consciousness, falling consciousness, moderate–severe headache, intoxication, skull fracture, other injury or abnormal CT (ICMR STW).
Others: discharge with head-injury advice and return precautions (ICMR STW).

regimens.dose: Adults 200 mL over 30 minutes; general dose 0.25–1 g/kg bolus
adjustments: Paediatric: Weight-based in children (0.25–1 g/kg) (ICMR STW).
Penicillin allergy: Not an antibiotic; penicillin allergy does not change this medicine.
CKD: Avoid or use with care in kidney failure (fluid shifts, acute kidney injury); monitor osmolality.
contraindications: Systolic BP 90 mmHg or below (ICMR STW)
